newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-AJAX SIGN DANISH OLSEN TO REPLACE VAN GAAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-AJAX SIGN DANISH OLSEN TO REPLACE VAN GAAL.

text.p: Dutch first division club Ajax Amsterdam have signed former Danish international Morten Olsen to replace Louis van Gaal as coach for the next two seasons.
Saturday's official announcement of Olsen's appointment, which takes effect from the start of next season, confirmed media reports last Wednesday tipping the Dane for the job.
Ajax, European champions in 1995 and beaten finalists last season, are currently languishing in seventh place in the league.
Olsen, 47, who played a record 102 games for Denmark, has had a brief and undistinguished managerial career.
He coached Danish club Brondby for two seasons before joining German first division side Cologne in 1992 -- the club where he ended his playing career aged almost 40.
After four seasons in charge and without a trophy to his name, Olsen was sacked in 1995.
The hugely successful Van Gaal announced late last year he planned to leave Ajax for fresh challenges, hinting he would seek a coaching job outside The Netherlands.
Van Gaal's decision prompted a flurry of speculation as to his likely successor, but illustrious names like Johan Cruyff, Marco van Basten and Kevin Keegan were overlooked by the Ajax board.
Olson began his playing career at Vordingborg in Denmark, before moving to Nykoping and then to Cercle Brugge, Molenbeek and Anderlecht in Belgium, ending a long and successful career at Cologne.
